key_concepts: Cellular respiration produces carbon dioxide as a byproduct.
Yeast, sugar, and warm water produce carbon dioxide through fermentation.
Warm temperatures support fermentation or cellular respiration.
Oxygen is needed for cellular respiration.
Mitochondria are the site of cellular respiration.
ATP is the energy currency of the cell.
Autotrophs convert carbon dioxide into sugar and oxygen.
Heterotrophs convert organic compounds into carbon dioxide and energy.
Cellular respiration produces six molecules each of carbon dioxide and water.
Bacteria are single-celled organisms without mitochondria.
